newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium issues warrants for minister's killers.
newsitem.headline: Belgium issues warrants for minister's killers.

text.p: Belgium has issued international arrest warrants for the two alleged assassins of leading politician Andre Cools, Belgian BRTN radio said on Monday.
It said that after the mafia-style murder the two men, of Tunisian origin, had travelled back to Sicily where their last address was known to police.
Cools, a former Socialist minister, was gunned down at point-blank range on July 18, 1991, outside his mistress's house near the eastern Belgian city of Liege.
BRTN said the assassins were aged 19 and 26 at the time. It was unclear whether they were still in Sicily or even whether they were still alive.
It said they had been living in the Agrigento region.
The Foreign Ministry had no comment on the radio report and Liege public prosecutors could not be reached for comment.
Six people, including former government minister Alain Van der Biest, have been arrested and charged with orchestrating Cools's murder.
Van der Biest denies any involvement in the killing.

The arrests came after an anonymous witness told police how a Belgo-Italian -- one of those arrested -- associated with organised crime had driven to Sicily to collect the killers. He later drove them back as well.
The witness also supplied other details of the preparations for the murder.

It remains unclear who ordered the killing or why, although the murder has been linked to an announcement by Cools that he would make revelations about corruption in the francophone Socialist Party at the end of the summer of 1991.
According to lawyers for some of the accused, witnesses told investigators the murder was a contract killing for 750,000 Belgian francs ($25,000).
Over the past five years the inquiry into Cools's death and the role he played as one of the bosses in the Socialist Party has uncovered corruption at the highest levels of Belgian government.
The scandal led to the resignation of four ministers and NATO Secretary General Willy Claes and the suicide of a top general.
